crime: Every dusk in the courtyard, {WITCH_NAME} raised her bare forearms, turned them to steel, and let a prisoner swing full cuts at them. The swordswoman was due to fight in a national tournament, and the ring of blade on steel carried across the courtyard to the lounge. When practice ended, she sat on alone against the tree until dark.

{WITCH_NAME} had grown up at her grandfather's anvil, judging steel by its ring. When he died, her mother sold the forge and all his blades. "Nobody here wants to hear a girl talk about steel." She never spoke of steel again.
One dusk, she ran her thumb along the notches all those cuts had left near the tip of the sword, and for the first time she spoke of steel. "My grandfather could have saved this edge."
The swordswoman laughed and raised the sword again. "It's only for swinging. You just be my wall."
{WITCH_NAME} stepped inside the cut and pressed the girl's face against her steel shoulder. The sword fell. Fists beat uselessly on steel, and she held on until the girl stopped.

She left the body sitting against the tree where the swordswoman always rested. Then she took up the sword and struck her own forearm in the practice rhythm, and the familiar ringing went on until the hour practice always ended. Moments after the last ring, she walked into the lounge and sat among the prisoners until the body was found at dark.
In the trial court, the prisoners ruled that the swordswoman had been smothered where she sat, after {WITCH_NAME} came in: the ringing had run until moments before she walked through the door.

Then a prisoner found fresh, bright nicks on the blade a hand's width from the guard, where no full cut ever lands. The court understood. {WITCH_NAME} had struck her own steel arm to ring out a practice for a dead girl.
fields.epitaph: Every dusk, someone came to make her ring, and all she ever heard was "wall."
execution: The execution stand raises her grandfather's forge, grown to giant size. Great tongs close around her waist and hold her above the hearth. They lay her into the coal bed as the bellows breathe it white. She hardens and beats at the tongs, and every blow rings out clear over the silent court. At last the ringing stops. The tongs hold her still in the dimming coals, and the bellows sigh to rest.

magic.name: Living Steel
magic.text: She can turn her body to living steel that no blade, blow or fall can hurt.
